items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1958-11-14
items.q: It was Willie Wilson, a fellow by the name of Santimo, and Landry.

ctx.x: Slide. Playing Slide. And a fellow by the name of Smith was playing Tramon. He was the manager of that band. He died too. And an old fellow by the name of Verrett was playing bass. And Alphonse, I can't call his other name, he was playing, he was a dog fellow, he was a pigeon toe playing the mellophone. And an old man by the name of Tico was playing the baritone. It was Willie Wilson, a fellow by the name of Santimo, and Landry. Big Al Landry. Oh yeah, Andrew Landry.
And on bass drum, let's see who was playing the bass drum.

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-11-25
items.q: And then Willie to Willie Ben. Willie Wilson.

ctx.x: So anyway, that was the first thing I wanted to ask you about, was about change of name, you know, Zeno, and when you changed it and why. Well, when I was born, my mother had several names, Francis, Joseph, Louis, Zeno. George was nowhere around. My mother had all the children that my mother had, two before me, they died. So my grandmother said, call this one George. My mother never had in her mind to call me George. But my grandma kept calling me George until my christening time when my mother went and had me…

I'll have to make it and play music, talk more with people and I find it's a good seat. So when Natalie was playing, he was playing, I was at the... I was playing my clarinet, same keys of trouble, but he didn't. Same keys of violin. Old shops and old flats. What about George like that? I would, a lot of him, I have a picture of him taking a job. Do you have a picture of yourself? Yeah, I remember Glenn, him, Bonk, me, him, Bonk, Marsman, Riley, Jim, and Dre, Elton, Mr. Tran, we played at the Academy of Music in…

Well, sometimes on those older records, they don't play 4-4, they play... What is it? Double record. Boy, at the night, there was a lot of people. Frank... Lauren, this is here, there was a lot of people. Sex. Go ahead and take the telephone. Lauren used to do it, a lot of times. And he kept... All the bands that I can show you, I know. Two men bands at the best time. You know that? It's a band of sales and... Or... Or the Kimber. Or the... Or the... Orubaloo. Orubaloo comes more... Closer, you don't know…
